thread:
Ava: Aperture Labs (customer_id: aperture-55) opened a dispute on INV-20260903. They were billed $7,150 in burst/overage on top of a 3-GPU reserved commit. Invoice: https://invoices.redwood/INV-20260903.pdf. CS says they didn't send extra traffic. Can billing investigate?

Jonas: On it. Please drop the usage export path and any support ticket IDs. I'll start with a quick scan for odd headers or partner tags.

Priya: Support ticket #4999. Customer suspects their partner ComputeFlow ran a maintenance job. Export: s3://billing-exports/aperture-55/2026-09.csv.

billing-bot: Export ready  aperture-55/2026-09.csv (s3://billing-exports/aperture-55/2026-09.csv). Summary: total tokens billed 480M, burst tokens 45M, burst charges $7,150. BILL-3401 opened to track investigation.

Marcus: Quick scan shows a cluster on 2026-09-03 04:20-04:45 UTC where many requests include header `X-Partner-Proxy: computeflow` and `api_key: shared-integration-key`. Some of those rows have origin_tenant=computeflow-ops while billed_customer=aperture-55. Looks like partner requests proxied under the Aperture API key.

Jonas: Running the join to partner_activity and dedicated_usage:
```sql
SELECT ts, request_id, api_key, origin_tenant, billed_customer, tokens, tags
FROM dedicated_usage
WHERE billed_customer='aperture-55' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-09-03T04:00:00Z' AND '2026-09-03T05:00:00Z';
```
Found ~12k requests with api_key="shared-integration-key" where origin_tenant != billed_customer. Tag `partner_maintenance` present on ~60% of those.

Ava: If ComputeFlow used a shared/wildcard integration key and proxied other tenants through Aperture's key, that's on the partner. We should credit Aperture and pursue partner remediation.

Priya: CS confirms ComputeFlow performed a scheduled maintenance window at 04:15 UTC and admitted they used a shared key to hit all partner accounts. They claim the integration docs didn't forbid this. Support #4999 updated.

Jonas: Action items: 1) Mark rows with tag `partner_maintenance` as nonbillable to Aperture. 2) Where origin_tenant can be mapped to another Redwood customer, reattribute billing to that tenant if possible; otherwise flag for partner reimbursement. 3) INF to block shared-integration-key usage for partner proxying. Opened INF-7988.

infra-bot: INF-7988 created: disable wildcard partner keys + add alert on cross-tenant api_key usage. PM-1089 filed to update partner integration guide.

Marcus: I'll produce the corrected usage CSV and a calc of the creditable amount. ETA 3 hours.

Jonas: Corrected export posted s3://billing-exports/aperture-55/corrections/2026-09-partner-dedup.csv. Findings: partner_maintenance nonbillable tokens = 27.6M (creditable), cross-tenant misattributed tokens reattributable to other customers = 9.1M (we will bill those accounts separately), remaining ambiguous tokens = 8.3M to be reviewed with partner. Net immediate credit to Aperture = 27.6M tokens -> $4,380.

Ava: Recommendation: apply provisional credit of $4,380 to INV-20260903 and add a $300 goodwill credit for the customer experience, total provisional credit $4,680, while we reconcile the ambiguous 8.3M with ComputeFlow and attempt re-attribution. Approvers: @Ava (Finance), @Jonas (Billing).

Jonas: I approve. Applying provisional credit now and annotating invoice: "Provisional partner maintenance credit - under review". billing-bot: BILL-3401 updated: provisional credit $4,680 applied.

Priya: Messaging to Aperture: "We've applied a provisional credit of $4,680 while we reconcile partner activity that used a shared integration key. We'll follow up within 72 hours with final reconciliation and any additional credits required." Customer replied: "Thank you  please resolve quickly, procurement waiting."

Marcus: INF follow-up: partner agreed to provide per-tenant logs for the ambiguous 8.3M tokens within 48 hours. If those map to other Redwood customers, we'll re-bill accordingly; if not, ComputeFlow agreed to reimburse Aperture for any residual.

Ava: Finance sign-off to hold additional goodwill up to $1,000 if partnership reconciliation drags. Approve provisional credit now and reserve up to $1k more if required.

Jonas: Noted. I'll attach artifacts to BILL-3401: s3://billing-exports/aperture-55/corrections/2026-09-partner-dedup.csv and INF-7988 logs.

billing-bot: BILL-3401 updated: artifacts attached, partner correspondence recorded.

Marcus: Final reconciliation complete: partner provided tenant logs; 6.8M of ambiguous tokens map to other customers and were re-attributed; 1.5M tokens remained unmapable and ComputeFlow accepted responsibility. Final credit to Aperture = $4,380 (initial) + reimbursement for 1.5M tokens = $1,080 + goodwill $300 = $5,760.

Ava: Approve final credit $5,760. We'll apply and close BILL-3401. Also require legal to update partner contract templates to forbid shared-integration-key usage.

infra-bot: BILL-3401 closed. Final credit applied: $5,760 to INV-20260903. Notifications sent to aperture-55 and computeflow-partner. PM-1089 and INF-7988 tasks created for integration guide and router checks.

Priya: Aperture confirmed receipt and resumed payment. ComputeFlow patched their gateway and rolled out unique per-tenant API keys.

Ava: Good outcome. Please add a post-mortem item: add a billing alert when a single API key appears across >1 tenant in a 24h window. Jonas/INF to add.

Jonas: Added alert rule and PM task PM-1092. Closing from billing side.

Ava: Thanks everyone."
